nuggets.text: Mississippi State's first mascot, Bully I, is buried beneath the players' bench at the 50-yard line of Davis Wade Stadium.
Legend says the Bulldogs' cowbells began when a jersey cow wandered onto the field during a home game against Ole Miss.
Cowbells were banned at Davis Wade Stadium from 1977 to 2009, and Bulldogs fans kept bringing them anyway.
Davis Wade Stadium opened in 1914 and is the second-oldest stadium in the FBS, behind only Georgia Tech's Bobby Dodd Stadium.
Scott Field is named for Donald Scott, an Olympic middle-distance runner who was a Bulldogs football star in 1915 and 1916.
Mississippi State's teams switched from the Aggies to the Maroons in 1932.
Kamario Taylor piled up 413 total yards and five touchdowns in the Bulldogs' 62-13 opener against UL Monroe.
The Bulldogs racked up 762 total yards in the opener, and 11 different players caught a pass.
Freshman J.J. Hill ran for 118 yards on just seven carries against UL Monroe, including a 57-yard touchdown.
Saturday is the first meeting ever between Mississippi State and Minnesota, an SEC vs. Big Ten showdown in Minneapolis.
